gaps: No NASA or FAA report with a hail-on-CFRP threshold table other than the FAA JAMS paper (Kim et al., UCSD) was reachable; the Kim and Kedward AIAA/UCSD dissertation PDFs (escholarship.org) returned 403 to curl, so their final FTE tables are unread. Table 8 here is an in-progress 2010 snapshot.

No hail threshold data for tubes, or for laminates under 1.5 mm, or for high-modulus (M55J, pitch) fibres; all hail data are flat quasi-isotropic panels 1.59-6 mm thick with 38-61 mm ice, energies 174-1400 J.
No threshold for 25 mm hail on CFRP found: smallest ice in the sourced threshold data is 38.1 mm.
No CAI row prints both an undamaged strength and a damaged strength at the same energy except Barile 2019 (385 vs 202 MPa, 50 J, 5 mm); retention ratios elsewhere are not printed.

Tube data: Mack and Tan print CAI results only in force-displacement figures (no strengths in text); the only printed retention ratios for tubes are RADIAL crush ratios (Xiao 2020), not axial. No axial residual strength after transverse impact, and no M55J/pitch tube impact data, found.

Hail properties: no ASTM F320, UL 2218, FAA or IEC 61215 standard text was obtained; mass of 25-51 mm hail only from a web FAQ (QUESTIONABLE). Heymsfield 2014 fit equations lose exponents in text extraction and were not recorded as numbers. Marshall paper year not printed in the extracted text.
Unread/unverified: Tang 2019 (JMRT), Liu 2022 (Eng Fract Mech), Hong 2009, Kim and Kedward 2000-2002 papers, Springer s40735-020-00458-4 (paywalled/redirect), NTRS 19880013566 (not opened).
